title_en: China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Guiyang Office v. Guiyang Kailin Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan contract
ruling_gist_en: The important distinction between joint and several liability suretyship and general suretyship is that: the surety under a general suretyship enjoys the right of preliminary objection (benefit of discussion), i.e., the creditor must first pursue the principal debtor and only after compulsory execution fails to satisfy the claim may the surety be required to bear the suretyship liability; whereas the surety under a joint and several liability suretyship does not enjoy that right. Where the statute of limitations for the guaranteed obligation has already commenced, the provisions on the guarantee period no longer apply.

full_text_en:
China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Guiyang Office v. Guiyang Kailin Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan contract

[Ruling Summary]

An important distinction between joint and several liability suretyship and general suretyship lies in the fact that: a surety under a general suretyship enjoys the right of objection prior to recourse, i.e., the creditor must first assert its rights against the principal debtor, and only after the principal debtor's property has been subject to compulsory enforcement and the debt remains unsatisfied may it require the surety to assume suretyship liability; whereas a surety under a joint and several liability suretyship does not enjoy the right of objection prior to recourse. When the statute of limitations has already commenced running for a secured debt, the provisions relating to the suretyship period shall no longer apply.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2008) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 106

Appellant (Plaintiff at first instance): China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Guiyang Office, domiciled at No. 42 Fushui North Road, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province.

Person in charge: Zhou Chengjie, Director of the Office.

Agent ad litem: Sun Shaosong, lawyer of Beijing Lifang Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at first instance): Guizhou Kailin Co., Ltd., address: 12th Floor, Haitian Commercial Building, No. 203 Zhonghua South Road, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province.

Legal representative: Qu Qinglin, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Gong Shiming, lawyer of Guilong Law Firm.

For the dispute over a loan contract between the appellant China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Guiyang Office (hereinafter referred to as Cinda Guiyang Office) and the respondent Guiyang Kailin Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kailin Company), the appellant appealed against the civil judgment (2007) Qian Gao Min Er Chu Zi No. 35 rendered by the Guizhou High People's Court to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with trial judge Qian Xiaochen presiding, and acting judges Liu Min and Yang Zhengyu participating, and clerk Yuan Hongxia keeping the record. The trial of this case has now concluded.

The Guizhou High People's Court found the following facts:

On October 6, 1989, the Central Sub-branch of the People's Construction Bank of China in the Qiannan Buyi and Miao Autonomous Prefecture (hereinafter referred to as Qiannan Central Sub-branch) entered into a contract numbered Qian Xin Zi No. 4 entitled "People's Construction Bank of China Capital Construction Loan Contract" with Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant, whereby Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant borrowed RMB 8 million from Qiannan Central Sub-branch, with the loan term from October 1989 to December 1996, and a repayment plan of: RMB 1 million in 1992, RMB 2 million in 1993, RMB 2 million in 1994, RMB 2 million in 1995, and RMB 1 million in December 1996, with interest calculated at an annual rate of 13.68%; if the borrower failed to repay according to the annual plan, the unreturned loan from the following year would be treated as overdue loan with an additional interest of 50%; if the interest rate changed due to national policy, the loan interest rate under this contract would be adjusted accordingly. Upon maturity of all loans, if the borrower failed to repay within three months after the lender issued an overdue notice, the lender could directly deduct from any investment or deposit of the borrower or the guarantor. Kailin Company affixed its seal in the column for the guaranteeing unit.

On August 7, 1990, Qiannan Central Sub-branch entered into a contract numbered Qian Xin Zi No. 5 entitled "People's Construction Bank of China Capital Construction Loan Contract" with Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant, whereby Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant borrowed RMB 6 million from Qiannan Central Sub-branch, with the loan term from August 30, 1995 to October 20, 1997. The repayment plan was: RMB 2 million in October 1995, RMB 1 million in June 1996, RMB 2 million in October 1996, and RMB 1 million in October 1997, with interest calculated at an annual rate of 8.64%; any portion that the borrower failed to repay according to the repayment plan stipulated in this contract would be treated as overdue and subject to an additional interest of 30%; if the interest rate changed due to national policy, the loan interest rate under this contract would be adjusted accordingly. If the loan matured and the borrower could not repay on time, the guaranteeing unit would repay on its behalf; if the guaranteeing unit failed to repay within three months after receiving the repayment notice from the lender, the lender could directly deduct from any investment or deposit of the borrower or the guaranteeing unit. Kailin Company affixed its seal in the column for the guaranteeing unit.

On June 18, 1991, Qiannan Central Sub-branch entered into a contract numbered (91) Dai Zi No. 009 entitled "People's Construction Bank of China Loan Contract" with Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant, stipulating that Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant would borrow RMB 3 million from Qiannan Central Sub-branch, with the loan term from June 18, 1991 to June 18, 1996. Interest was calculated at an annual rate of 7.02%; any portion that the borrower failed to repay according to this contract would be treated as overdue and subject to an additional interest of 20%; if the interest rate changed due to national policy, the loan interest rate under this contract would be adjusted accordingly. If the loan matured and the borrower could not repay on time, the guaranteeing unit would repay on its behalf; if the guaranteeing unit failed to repay within three months after receiving the repayment notice from Qiannan Central Sub-branch, Qiannan Central Sub-branch had the right to deduct from the investment or deposit accounts of the borrower or the guaranteeing unit, or to entrust other financial institutions to do so. Kailin Company affixed its seal in the column for the guaranteeing unit.

On June 27, 1992, Qiannan Central Sub-branch entered into a contract numbered (92) Jian Dai Zi No. 2 entitled "People's Construction Bank of China Loan Contract" with Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant, stipulating that Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant would borrow RMB 3.5 million from Qiannan Central Sub-branch, with the loan term from June 27, 1992 to June 26, 1999. Interest was calculated at an annual rate of 7.20%; any portion that the borrower failed to repay according to this contract would be treated as overdue and subject to an additional interest of 20%; if the interest rate changed due to national policy, the loan interest rate under this contract would be adjusted accordingly. If the loan matured and the borrower could not repay on time, the guaranteeing unit would repay on its behalf; if the guaranteeing unit failed to repay within three months after receiving the repayment notice from Qiannan Central Sub-branch, Qiannan Central Sub-branch had the right to deduct from the investment or deposit accounts of the borrower or the guaranteeing unit, or to entrust other financial institutions to do so. Kailin Company affixed its seal in the column for the guaranteeing unit.

On October 15, 1993, Qiannan Central Sub-branch entered into a contract numbered (93) Yun Jian Dai Zi No. 2 entitled "People's Construction Bank of China Loan Contract" with Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant, stipulating that Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant would borrow RMB 4 million from Qiannan Central Sub-branch, with the loan term from October 22, 1993 to October 21, 1999. Interest was calculated at an annual rate of 9.9%; any portion that the borrower failed to repay according to this contract would be treated as overdue and subject to an additional interest of 20%; if the interest rate changed due to national policy, the loan interest rate under this contract would be adjusted accordingly. If the loan matured and the borrower could not repay on time, the guaranteeing unit would repay on its behalf; if the guaranteeing unit failed to repay within three months after receiving the repayment notice from Qiannan Central Sub-branch, Qiannan Central Sub-branch had the right to deduct from the investment or deposit accounts of the borrower or the guaranteeing unit, or to entrust other financial institutions to do so. Kailin Company affixed its seal in the column for the guaranteeing unit. On the same day, Kailin Company also issued a "Loan Guarantee Letter" to Qiannan Central Sub-branch, undertaking that "when the borrowing unit is unable to perform the loan contract and repay the principal and interest on time, this company (factory) will unconditionally assume responsibility and guarantee to repay the outstanding principal and interest owed by the borrowing unit in accordance with the provisions of the loan contract. This guarantee letter is irrevocable. This guarantee letter is an ancillary document to Loan Contract No. (93) Yun Jian Dai Zi No. 2, and its validity shall last until all principal and interest repayable by the borrowing unit are fully repaid."

After the above contracts were signed, Qiannan Central Sub-branch disbursed the loans as agreed, but Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant failed to repay them. On December 4, 1999, Qiannan Central Sub-branch assigned the above claims to China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Chongqing Office, and on December 8, 1999, served a "Notice of Transfer of Security Rights" on the guarantor Kailin Company, which noted on the receipt: "The loan guarantee period has expired, and our company no longer assumes guarantee liability." China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Chongqing Office, which received the assignment of the claims, further assigned the above claims to Cinda Guiyang Office on March 27, 2001. Cinda Guiyang Office published announcements in the Guizhou Daily on July 17, 2001, September 17, 2001, August 8, 2003, May 21, 2005, and May 15, 2007, claiming the above debts against the borrower and the guarantor. On October 2, 2001, Cinda Guiyang Office also served a "Notice of Performance of Guarantee Obligation" on Kailin Company, which noted on the receipt: "The original guarantee was arranged by the Chemical Industry Department and has already lapsed. Our company no longer assumes the guarantee obligation for this debt. See the attachment for specific receipt content." On August 1, 2003, Cinda Guiyang Office served a "Notice of Performance of Guarantee Obligation" on Kailin Company by notarized delivery. Kailin Company did not sign for this notice.

On December 24, 2004, the Qiannan Buyi and Miao Autonomous Prefecture Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Qiannan Intermediate Court) legally ruled to declare Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant bankrupt for debt repayment, and on December 22, 2005, issued a civil ruling (2004) Qiannan Min Er Po Zi No. 1-2, ruling the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings of the principal debtor Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant. On December 26, 2005, it posted a notice of the conclusion of the bankruptcy and debt repayment proceedings of Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant on the court's bulletin board, and on January 17, 2006, published the notice again in the People's Court Daily. On June 25, 2007, Cinda Guiyang Office received the civil ruling (2004) Qiannan Min Er Po Zi No. 1-2 from the Qiannan Intermediate Court and signed the service receipt for that ruling. On November 2, 2007, Cinda Guiyang Office filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting a judgment ordering Kailin Company to perform its guarantee liability and repay the principal and interest of the loans owed by the guaranteed party Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant, totaling RMB 72,381,616.50. At the trial in the court of first instance, Cinda Guiyang Office argued that it only learned of the conclusion of Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant's bankruptcy on June 25, 2007, when it received the civil ruling (2004) Qiannan Min Er Po Zi No. 1-2 from the Qiannan Intermediate Court, and that this date should be the starting point for calculating the statute of limitations for its claim against Kailin Company for the guarantee debt.

The Guizhou High People's Court held that: The Loan Contracts numbered Qian Xin Zi No. 4, Qian Xin Zi No. 5, (91) Dai Zi No. 009, (92) Jian Dai Zi No. 2, and (93) Yun Jian Dai Zi No. 2, as well as the Loan Guarantee Letter issued by Kailin Company, entered into between Qiannan Central Sub-branch, Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant, and Kailin Company, represented the true intentions of the three parties and did not violate relevant laws, and therefore should be valid. The above contracts were all signed before the promulgation and implementation of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, and the relevant provisions of Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Issues Concerning Guarantees in the Trial of Economic Contract Disputes" (Fa Fa [1994] No. 8, hereinafter referred to as Document No. 8) should apply to determine the guarantee method, guarantee period, and validity of the guarantees involved in the contracts. Since none of the above contracts clearly specified the method of guarantee liability to be borne by the guarantor Kailin Company, according to Article 7 of Document No. 8, which provides that "if a guarantee contract does not stipulate the type of liability to be borne by the guarantor, or if the stipulation is unclear, the guarantor shall be deemed to bear liability for compensation. When the guaranteed party fails to perform the contract upon maturity, the creditor shall first request the guaranteed party to discharge the debt. If the property of the guaranteed party after compulsory enforcement is still insufficient to satisfy the debt, the guarantor shall bear liability for compensation," and according to Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Reply on the Application of Judicial Interpretations Concerning Guarantee Disputes and the Determination of the Method of Guarantee Liability," which provides that "for guarantee contracts concluded before the Security Law came into effect, if the method of guarantee liability is not stipulated or is unclear, it shall be deemed as a general suretyship," the guarantee liability of Kailin Company should be determined as a general suretyship. Since the parties also did not stipulate a suretyship period in the contracts, or did not clearly stipulate one, according to Article 11 of Document No. 8, which provides that "if a guarantee contract does not stipulate a guarantee liability period, or the stipulation is unclear, the guarantor shall bear guarantee liability within the period during which the guaranteed party bears liability," for the loans borrowed by Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant on October 6, 1989 (RMB 8 million), August 7, 1990 (RMB 6 million), and June 18, 1991 (RMB 3 million), the maturity dates were December 1996, October 20, 1997, and June 18, 1996, respectively. Therefore, the period for the guarantor to bear guarantee liability should be the two-year statute of limitations period, i.e., from December 31, 1996 to December 31, 1998, from October 21, 1997 to October 20, 1999, and from June 19, 1996 to June 18, 1998, respectively. Within the above guarantee periods, Cinda Guiyang Office did not assert its rights against Kailin Company to require it to bear corresponding guarantee liability for these three debts. When it first asserted its rights against Kailin Company on December 8, 1999, by means of a "Notice of Transfer of Security Rights," the statutory guarantee period had already expired, and Kailin Company twice expressly refused to continue to bear guarantee liability for the above debts in the "Receipt for Notice of Transfer of Security Rights" and the "Notice of Performance of Guarantee Obligation." Therefore, Kailin Company's guarantee liability for the debts under these three loan contracts had been legally discharged. Cinda Guiyang Office's request that Kailin Company bear guarantee liability for these three debts has no legal basis, and the court does not support it. For the loans borrowed by Kailin Company on June 27, 1992 (RMB 3.5 million) and on October 22, 1993 (RMB 4 million), the maturity dates were June 26, 1999 and October 21, 1999, respectively. Therefore, the guarantee periods for these two debts were from June 27, 1999 to June 26, 2001, and from October 22, 1999 to October 21, 2001, respectively. When Cinda Guiyang Office asserted its rights against Kailin Company on December 8, 1999, by means of a "Notice of Transfer of Security Rights," it did so within the effective guarantee period. Therefore, the statute of limitations for its claim for the guarantee debt against Kailin Company was interrupted. Thereafter, within the statute of limitations period, Cinda Guiyang Office published debt collection announcements in the Guizhou Daily to assert its rights against Kailin Company, and also served "Notices of Performance of Guarantee Obligation" on Kailin Company by direct delivery and notarized delivery on October 2, 2001 and August 1, 2003, respectively, requiring Kailin Company to assume guarantee liability. Therefore, the statute of limitations for these two guarantee debts was interrupted multiple times by the above collection actions. On December 24, 2004, the Qiannan Intermediate Court legally ruled that the debtor for these two loans, Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant, should be subject to bankruptcy and debt repayment. Cinda Guiyang Office filed a claim for the five debts involved in this case as bankruptcy claims, but received no satisfaction due to a zero repayment rate. According to Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Notice on Issues Concerning the Guarantee Period for Guarantee Acts Occurring Before the Security Law Came into Effect" (Fa [2002] No. 144, hereinafter referred to as Document No. 144), which provides that "if the principal debtor enters bankruptcy proceedings and the creditor has not filed a claim, the creditor may also assert its claim against the guarantor within the aforementioned period; if the creditor has already filed a claim, for the portion of the claim not satisfied in the bankruptcy proceedings, the creditor may assert its claim against the guarantor within six months after the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings," Cinda Guiyang Office should have asserted its claim against Kailin Company within six months after the conclusion of Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant's bankruptcy proceedings. Regarding the time of conclusion of the bankruptcy, since the Qiannan Intermediate Court published the bankruptcy conclusion notice in the People's Court Daily on January 17, 2006, that date should be the date on which all bankruptcy creditors became aware of the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings. Therefore, that date should be the starting point for calculating the statute of limitations period, i.e., Cinda Guiyang Office should have asserted its claim for the guarantee debt against Kailin Company during the period from January 18, 2006 to July 17, 2006. Cinda Guiyang Office's argument that the date it received the civil ruling (2004) Qiannan Min Er Po Zi No. 1-2 from the Qiannan Intermediate Court on June 25, 2007, should be the date it learned of the conclusion of Kailin Company's bankruptcy, and that this should be the starting point for calculating the statute of limitations for its claim against Kailin Company, and that its lawsuit filed on November 2, 2007, was within six months after the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings, so its claim should be supported. The court, upon review, held that when the Qiannan Intermediate Court ruled on December 22, 2005, to conclude the bankruptcy proceedings of Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant, the laws and regulations in effect at that time did not require the people's court to serve a bankruptcy conclusion ruling on bankruptcy creditors, nor did they specify the method by which the people's court should inform bankruptcy creditors of the conclusion of bankruptcy proceedings. Therefore, the Qiannan Intermediate Court's use of a public notice to inform bankruptcy creditors of the conclusion of bankruptcy proceedings was not improper. Cinda Guiyang Office should have become aware of the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings after the notice was published, and therefore should have asserted its claim against the guarantor within the prescribed effective period, i.e., before July 17, 2006. Although Cinda Guiyang Office received the civil ruling on the conclusion of bankruptcy on June 25, 2007, that act could not produce the legal effect of restarting the statute of limitations period. Therefore, when it filed a lawsuit with the court on November 2, 2007, to assert its claim for the guarantee debt against Kailin Company, the statute of limitations period under Article 2 of Document No. 144 had already expired, and it had lost its right of action in accordance with the law. Thus, Kailin Company's guarantee liability had been legally discharged. Therefore, Cinda Guiyang Office's above argument has no legal basis, and the court of first instance rejected it in accordance with the law. Kailin Company's defense argument that Cinda Guiyang Office's lawsuit filed on November 2, 2007, exceeded the statutory statute of limitations period, and therefore its guarantee liability for the above debts should be discharged, was supported by the court. The Guizhou High People's Court, in accordance with Article 64(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 7 and 11 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Issues Concerning Guarantees in the Trial of Economic Contract Disputes," Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Reply on the Application of Judicial Interpretations Concerning Guarantee Disputes and the Determination of the Method of Guarantee Liability," and Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Notice on Issues Concerning the Guarantee Period for Guarantee Acts Occurring Before the Security Law Came into Effect," ruled: Cinda Guiyang Office's claim was dismissed; the case acceptance fee of RMB 201,854.04 was borne by Cinda Guiyang Office.

Appellant Xinda Company Guiyang Office, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court stating: 1. For guarantee contracts concluded before the effectiveness of the Guarantee Law which did not stipulate a guarantee period, the period for the guarantor to assume liability should be until the loan principal and interest are fully repaid. The court of first instance misinterpreted the phrase "the period during which the guaranteed person assumes guarantee liability" in Article 11 of the No. 8 Document as the two-year limitation of action period after the expiration of the performance period of the principal contract. The No. 144 Document clearly provides that for guarantee contracts concluded before the effectiveness of the Guarantee Law which did not stipulate a guarantee period, and where the limitation of action for the principal debt remained valid but no claim was made against the guarantor, the creditor should assert rights against the guarantor during the period "from August 1, 2002 to January 31, 2003." The period "from August 1, 2002 to January 31, 2003" is the "guarantee period" for guarantee contracts concluded before the effectiveness of the Guarantee Law which did not stipulate a guarantee period and where no claim was made against the guarantor. In this case, the Appellant asserted rights against the guarantor on December 8, 1999, and thereafter made annual demands for repayment. According to Articles 11 and 29 of the No. 8 Document, the Appellee should assume guarantee liability to the Appellant from December 8, 1999, when China Xinda Asset Management Corporation Chongqing Office first asserted rights against it, within the limitation of action. 2. The "six-month" period in Article 2 of the No. 144 Document, during which the creditor may assert claims against the guarantor for unsatisfied claims within six months after the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings, is not a limitation of action period. This article applies to guarantee contracts concluded before the effectiveness of the Guarantee Law where the creditor has asserted rights against the principal debtor within the statutory period but has not asserted rights against the guarantor. Since the Appellant has been asserting rights against the guarantor since December 8, 1999, this article should not apply. 3. The court of first instance incorrectly determined the guarantee liability method for the five loan contracts as general guarantee. According to Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Reply on the Application of Judicial Interpretations Concerning Guarantee Dispute Cases and the Determination of Guarantee Liability Methods," which states "...where a guarantee contract clearly stipulates that the guarantor assumes liability when the guaranteed person fails to perform the debt, and where a general guarantee liability cannot be inferred from the guarantor's intention in concluding the contract, it shall be deemed as joint and several guarantee liability." In the loan contracts signed between Qiannan Central Sub-branch and Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant for the borrowings of RMB 6 million on August 7, 1990, RMB 3 million on June 18, 1991, RMB 3 million on June 27, 1992, and RMB 4 million on October 15, 1993, Article 5 of each contract contains an agreement that "upon maturity of the loan, if Party A fails to repay on time, the guaranteeing unit shall repay on its behalf." Additionally, for the loan contract of October 15, 1993, the defendant also provided a guarantee letter clearly stating that when the borrower fails to perform its repayment obligation, the guarantor shall repay the loan principal and interest on behalf of the borrower. These four contracts comply with Article 2 of the above Reply, and the Appellee's guarantee liability method for these four contracts should be joint and several guarantee. 4. The Appellant only learned that the debtor, Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant, had concluded its bankruptcy proceedings upon receiving the bankruptcy termination ruling from Qiannan Intermediate People's Court. When declaring its bankruptcy claims, the Appellant submitted a detailed declaration to Qiannan Intermediate People's Court. There is no evidence indicating that the Appellant knew of the conclusion of the debtor's bankruptcy proceedings before June 25, 2007. A court should naturally notify known creditors in writing of the conclusion of the debtor's bankruptcy proceedings. The court of first instance was incorrect in taking the date of the court's public announcement as the date of service. We request that this Court cancel the judgment of first instance in accordance with the law, and order Kailin Company to perform its guarantee liability to the Appellant and repay on behalf of the guaranteed person, Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant, the outstanding principal and interest totaling RMB 72,381,616.5; and that the litigation costs of the first and second instances be borne by the Appellee.

Kailin Company argued in defense: 1. The guarantee periods for the five loan contracts in this case should be governed by the provisions of the No. 144 Document, specifically the period from August 1, 2002 to January 31, 2003. Because the Appellant did not assert rights against Kailin Company during that period, Kailin Company no longer bears guarantee liability. First, the No. 144 Document is a special interpretation and provision made to determine the guarantee period for guarantee acts that occurred before the implementation of the Guarantee Law, and it supplements the No. 44 Document [Fa (2000) No. 44] and the No. 8 Document. Therefore, whether under the principle that "special provisions prevail over general provisions" or that "later provisions prevail over earlier provisions," the No. 144 Document should apply. Second, according to the reply of the Supreme People's Court on November 28, 2003, to the request for instructions of Gansu High People's Court (Gan Gao Fa [2003] No. 183): "The phrase 'who have not asserted rights against the guarantor' in Article 1 of our court's No. 144 Document issued on August 1, 2002, is a description of the status of the debts transferred to the four asset management companies, including China Xinda Asset Management Corporation, and is not a necessary condition for the application of that notice. Therefore, for 'guarantee contracts concluded before the effectiveness of the Guarantee Law which did not stipulate a guarantee period or had unclear stipulations,' as long as 'the limitation of action for the principal debt has not expired,' regardless of whether the creditor has asserted rights against the guarantor, the creditor may assert rights against the guarantor in accordance with the provisions of the No. 144 Document." From this, even though the Appellant asserted rights against Kailin Company on December 8, 1999, and made subsequent demands, it still should have asserted rights against Kailin Company between August 1, 2002 and January 31, 2003, in accordance with the No. 144 Document. 2. Kailin Company's guarantee liability method for the five loan contracts is general guarantee. The guarantee acts for the five loan contracts all occurred before October 1, 1995, the effective date of the Guarantee Law of the PRC. Except for the first contract, which did not stipulate the guarantee liability method, the remaining four contracts all provided that "the guaranteeing unit shall repay on behalf of the borrower." According to Articles 5 and 7 of the No. 8 Document and Article 2 of the "Reply," the guarantee liability method for Kailin Company in this case should be general guarantee. 3. The date of the termination of the bankruptcy proceedings, as stated in the (2004) Qiannan Min Er Po Zi No. 1-2 civil ruling, should not be the date when the Appellant signed for receipt of that ruling. Qiannan Intermediate People's Court lawfully ruled on December 22, 2005, to terminate the bankruptcy proceedings of Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant, and on December 26, 2005, published a notice of the termination of the bankruptcy proceedings of Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant on the court's notice board, and again published such notice in the People's Court Daily on January 17, 2006. However, the Appellant, more than one year and a half after that ruling, went to Qiannan Intermediate People's Court on June 25, 2007, to sign for receipt of the ruling, with the intention of circumventing the statutory time limit for asserting rights against Kailin Company. According to the Bankruptcy Law of the PRC (for Trial Implementation) and the Supreme People's Court's "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Bankruptcy Law of the PRC (for Trial Implementation)," there is no provision that a court must serve the bankruptcy termination ruling to relevant creditors, nor any provision that the bankruptcy termination ruling takes legal effect only upon receipt by the creditor. 4. Since the Appellant failed to assert rights within the statutory period, Kailin Company no longer bears guarantee liability. (1) The guarantee liability method for all five loan contracts is general guarantee. According to Article 25 of the Guarantee Law, since the repayment periods for these five loan contracts have expired for eight to twelve years, and the Appellant has not filed a lawsuit or initiated arbitration against the principal debtor (borrower), Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant, Kailin Company is accordingly exempted from guarantee liability. (2) The five loan contracts and guarantee clauses were signed between October 1989 and October 1993, without stipulating a guarantee period. The No. 144 Document clearly provides for cases similar to this one and grants the asset management companies a reasonable period for judicial remedy. According to the spirit of this notice, the full period during which Kailin Company bears guarantee liability in this case should extend until January 31, 2003. However, the Appellant still failed to assert rights against Kailin Company in accordance with the law during the final judicial remedy period granted by the Supreme People's Court to the asset management companies (August 1, 2002 to January 31, 2003). Therefore, Kailin Company no longer bears guarantee liability. (3) The borrower under the five loan contracts, Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant, entered bankruptcy repayment proceedings on December 24, 2004, which was not within the six-month period (August 1, 2002 to January 31, 2003) provided in the No. 144 Document; by that time, the guarantee period had already expired. Therefore, the guarantee period in this case should not be extended to within six months after the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings of Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant pursuant to Article 2 of that notice. Moreover, even if the Appellant could rely on Article 2 of the No. 144 Document to assert rights against Kailin Company again, the Appellant should have done so, in accordance with that article and Article 44, Paragraph 2, of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the PRC" of September 29, 2000, within six months after the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings of Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant on December 22, 2005, i.e., by June 22, 2006. However, the Appellant asserted rights against Kailin Company nearly two years after the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings (on November 2, 2007), which also exceeded the time limit for asserting rights. Therefore, Kailin Company no longer bears guarantee liability. 5. The evidence submitted by the Appellant at the second instance, the Notarial Certificate (2003) Zhu Gong Min Zi No. 1118, should not be admitted as evidence in this case. The content certified by this notarial certificate is untrue; the service and abandonment were not made to Kailin Company but to Kaiyang Phosphate Mine Bureau, which had already been canceled in 1996, so the content is untrue. This notarial certificate was issued on January 2, 2003. The Appellant has been in possession of it since that time; it is not new evidence and was not presented to the court at the first instance. It should not be admitted. Therefore, we request that this Court dismiss the Appellant's appeal, uphold the judgment of first instance, and order the Appellant to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Facts found by this Court upon trial: In the loan contracts signed between Qiannan Central Sub-branch and Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant and Kailin Company, namely the Loan Contracts numbered Qian Xin Zi No. 4, Qian Xin Zi No. 5, (91) Dai Zi No. 009, (92) Jian Dai Zi No. 2, and (93) Yun Jian Dai Zi No. 2, the guaranteeing unit was sealed by Guiyang Phosphate Mine Bureau of Guizhou. On September 26, 1995, the People's Government of Guizhou Province and the State Economic and Trade Commission issued Qian Fu Han [1995] No. 175, "Reply on Approving the Implementation Plan for the Pilot Project of Establishing a Modern Enterprise System by Guiyang Phosphate Mine Bureau of Guizhou," approving that Guiyang Phosphate Mine Bureau of Guizhou should be restructured into a wholly state-owned company in accordance with the Company Law of the PRC, and renamed as "Guizhou Kailin (Group) Co., Ltd." On January 10, 1996, Guizhou Kailin (Group) Co., Ltd. issued a document stating that the former Guiyang Phosphate Mine Bureau of Guizhou had been restructured into a wholly state-owned company, renamed as Guizhou Kailin (Group) Co., Ltd., and its subordinate units and departments were also renamed accordingly. On August 16, 2005, Kailin Company announced: "With the approval of the State Council, Guizhou Kailin (Group) Co., Ltd. implemented a debt-to-equity swap on March 31, 2005, with shareholders being the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the People's Government of Guizhou Province, China Xinda Asset Management Corporation, China Huarong Asset Management Corporation, China Orient Asset Management Corporation, and China Haohua Chemical (Group) Corporation. The newly established company after the debt-to-equity swap is registered with the industry and commerce authority under the name 'Guizhou Kailin Co., Ltd.' The debts and claims of the former Guizhou Kailin (Group) Co., Ltd. are inherited by the new company, 'Guizhou Kailin Co., Ltd.'"

On January 2, 2003, the Guiyang Notary Public Office of Guizhou Province, upon the application of Xinda Company Guiyang Office, issued Notarial Certificate (2003) Zhu Gong Min Zi No. 1118, stating that Notary Public Qin Qiong of the Notary Office and Deng Qun, the agent ad litem of Xinda Company Guiyang Office, went together to Kaiyang Phosphate Mine Bureau at 9:30 a.m. on December 16, 2002. Deng Qun, in the presence of the notary public, served the Notice on Performance of Guarantee Obligations No. 2002-022 on the staff working in the office of Kaiyang Phosphate Mine Bureau, and the staff refused to sign for receipt. Deng Qun left the notice at the office of Kaiyang Phosphate Mine Bureau. The guarantee debts referred to in Notice No. 2002-022 are the debts in dispute in this case. On August 2, 2003, the Guiyang Notary Public Office of Guizhou Province, upon the application of Xinda Company Guiyang Office, issued Notarial Certificate (2003) Zhu Gong Min Zi No. 3771, stating that Notary Public Qin Qiong and Deng Qun, agent ad litem of Xinda Company Guiyang Office, went together to the office of Guizhou Kailin Group Co., Ltd. at 9:30 a.m. on August 1, 2003. Deng Qun served the Notice on Performance of Guarantee Obligations No. 2003-220 on a staff member working in the office of the company, and the staff member refused to sign for receipt. Deng Qun left the notice at the office of Guizhou Kailin Group Co., Ltd. The guarantee debts referred to in Notice No. 2003-220 are the debts in dispute in this case.

This Court confirms the other facts found by the court of first instance.

Opinion of this Court: The issues in dispute in this case are, first, the type of guarantee provided by Kailin Company, and second, whether Xinda Company Guiyang Office asserted rights against the guarantor Kailin Company within the period prescribed by law or judicial interpretation.

1. Regarding the method of guarantee provided by Kailin Company in this case

In this case, the guarantee provided by Kailin Company was expressed in two ways in the loan contracts: First, in the Loan Contract No. Qian Xin Zi No. 4, it stated: "If all loans become due and the lender issues a notice of overdue payment, and after three months the loan remains unpaid, the lender may directly deduct from various investments and deposits of the borrower or the guarantor." Second, in the Loan Contracts No. Qian Xin Zi No. 5, (91) Dai Zi No. 009, (92) Jian Dai Zi No. 2, and (93) Yun Jian Dai Zi No. 2, it stated: "Upon maturity of the loan, if the borrower fails to repay on time, the guaranteeing unit shall repay on its behalf. If the guaranteeing unit fails to repay within three months after receiving a repayment notice from Qiannan Central Sub-branch, Qiannan Central Sub-branch has the right to deduct from the investment or deposit accounts of the borrower or the guaranteeing unit, or authorize other financial institutions to do so." Additionally, Kailin Company issued a "Loan Guarantee Letter" to Qiannan Central Sub-branch regarding Loan Contract No. (93) Yun Jian Dai Zi No. 2, undertaking that "when the borrowing unit fails to perform the loan contract and repay the loan principal and interest on time, our company (factory) shall unconditionally assume responsibility and guarantee to repay the loan principal and interest owed on behalf of the borrowing unit in accordance with the provisions of the loan contract. This guarantee letter is irrevocable. This guarantee letter is an appendix to Loan Contract No. (93) Yun Jian Dai Zi No. 2, and its validity period extends until the borrowing unit has fully repaid the loan principal and interest." The important marker for distinguishing between joint and several guarantee and general guarantee is whether the guarantor enjoys the right of first objection, that is, whether the creditor must first assert rights against the principal debtor and obtain execution before being able to require the guarantor to assume guarantee liability. The first expression in the above loan contracts treats the liability of the guaranteeing party and the borrowing party together as soon as the loan reaches the agreed maturity and remains unpaid, without distinguishing whether the guarantor should assume guarantee liability only after the principal debtor is objectively unable to repay, that is, after the creditor has first sought recovery from the principal debtor without success. Therefore, the guarantee liability is clearly stipulated here as joint and several guarantee. The second expression in the above loan contracts contains the word "cannot." If the word "cannot" is used alone, it may imply an objective lack of capacity of the debtor to repay, in which case the guarantor's assumption of guarantee liability could be deemed as general guarantee. However, when the word "cannot" is combined with the phrase "on time," it cannot be interpreted as a stipulation of the objective inability to repay the loan; it merely indicates that guarantee liability arises upon failure to repay at maturity. Therefore, the second expression should also be determined as joint and several guarantee liability. As for the "Loan Guarantee Letter" provided by Kailin Company for Loan Contract No. (93) Yun Jian Dai Zi No. 2, it more clearly defines the guarantee liability as unconditional assumption, which is also a clearly stipulated joint and several guarantee. In summary, the guarantee liability in dispute in this case is joint and several guarantee liability. Since the principal debtor Guizhou Jianjiang Chemical Fertilizer Plant has already been bankrupted and the bankruptcy proceedings have concluded, even if the loan contracts had stipulated general guarantee liability, the guarantor's liability would have already arisen by reason of the principal debtor's bankruptcy.

2. Regarding whether Xinda Company Guiyang Office asserted rights against the guarantor Kailin Company within the statutory period

Since the loan contracts in dispute in this case were concluded before the implementation of the Guarantee Law of the PRC, the court of first instance correctly applied the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Issues Concerning Guarantee in the Trial of Economic Contract Dispute Cases" (Fa Fa [1994] No. 8) and the Supreme People's Court's "Notice on Issues Concerning the Guarantee Period for Guarantee Acts Occurring Before the Effectiveness of the Guarantee Law" (Fa [2002] No. 144) to determine the guarantee period in this case. However, the court of first instance misinterpreted the No. 144 Document in determining the guarantee period.

For the present case, the periods during which the Qiannan Central Sub-branch asserted claims against Kailin Company are divided into two categories. First, with respect to the Loan Contracts numbered Qianxin No. 4, Qianxin No. 5, and (91) Loan No. 009, the Qiannan Central Sub-branch did not assert claims against the guarantor, Kailin Company, within the two-year period in which the principal debtor was liable for performance. Second, with respect to the Loan Contracts numbered (92) Jian Dai No. 2 and (93) Yun Jian Dai No. 2, the Qiannan Central Sub-branch asserted claims against the guarantor, Kailin Company, within the two-year period in which the principal debtor was liable for performance. For the first category, although the Qiannan Central Sub-branch did not assert claims against Kailin Company within the warranty period, after it transferred the creditor's rights to the Guiyang Office of Xinda Company, the Guiyang Office could assert claims against the guarantor, Kailin Company, during the six-month period from August 1, 2002, to January 31, 2003, as specified in Document No. 144. Whether the Guiyang Office of Xinda Company asserted claims against Kailin Company within the aforementioned period is a question of fact in this case. After the court of first instance, based on Document No. 8 and Document No. 144, rendered a judgment discharging Kailin Company from its guarantor liability for the three loans described above, the Guiyang Office of Xinda Company, during the trial before this Court, presented, in response to the findings of the court of first instance and to demonstrate that it had asserted claims against the guarantor within the period specified in Document No. 144, a notarial certificate, (2003) Zhu Gong Min Zi No. 1118, issued by the Guiyang Notary Public Office of Guizhou Province, which constitutes new evidence. Although the full name of the guarantor listed in the "Notice of Fulfillment of Guaranty Obligations" attached to the notarial certificate was Kaiyang Phosphate Mine Administration, which had previously been renamed as Guizhou Kailin (Group) Co., Ltd., the continuity of the entity from beginning to end does not cause confusion as to the identity of the guarantor, and it also demonstrates that the Guiyang Office of Xinda Company asserted claims within the period specified in Document No. 144. Therefore, the facts certified by the notarial certificate should be confirmed, namely that the Guiyang Office of Xinda Company asserted claims against Kailin Company within the period specified in Document No. 144, with the statute of limitations commencing on December 12, 2002. For the second category, the Qiannan Central Sub-branch asserted claims against the guarantor, Kailin Company, within the two-year period in which the principal debtor was liable for performance, and the statute of limitations began to run from the date of such assertion. The provision in Article 2 of Document No. 144 that "the creditor may assert claims against the guarantor within six months after the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings" remains a continuation of the six-month warranty period specified in Article 1 of Document No. 144. Where the statute of limitations has already commenced in respect of the disputed loans, there is no need to further apply the six-month warranty period. Since, after the statute of limitations began to run for both categories, the Qiannan Central Sub-branch and the Guiyang Office of Xinda Company continuously asserted claims, causing the statute of limitations to be interrupted multiple times, the court of first instance improperly dismissed the claims on the ground that the Guiyang Office of Xinda Company had not asserted claims against the guarantor, Kailin Company, within the statutory period.

In summary, with respect to the guaranteed creditor's rights asserted by the Guiyang Office of Xinda Company against Kailin Company, because the creditor asserted claims against the guarantor within the statutory period, the defense of Kailin Company that it should not bear guarantor liability cannot be sustained. Kailin Company shall repay to the Guiyang Office of Xinda Company the principal of RMB 24,500,000 and interest of RMB 47,881,616.5, totaling RMB 72,381,616.5 in debt, up to the date of the Guiyang Office of Xinda Company's filing of the lawsuit. The court of first instance made unclear findings of fact and improperly applied the law. Therefore, in accordance with subparagraphs (2) and (3) of paragraph 1 of Article 153 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court orders as follows:

1. The Civil Judgment (2007) Qian Gao Min Er Chu Zi No. 35 of the Guizhou High People's Court is set aside.

2. Within 30 days from the date this judgment takes effect, Guizhou Kailin Co., Ltd. shall pay RMB 72,381,616.5 to the Guiyang Office of China Xinda Asset Management Corporation.

If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The court acceptance fees for the first and second instances are each RMB 201,854.04, to be borne by Guizhou Kailin Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
